summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues teaching about the conditions of salah, specifically focusing on the rules of covering the 'awrah (private parts) in Islamic dress. He outlines eight scholarly conditions for Islamic dress for both men and women, covering requirements such as complete body coverage, appropriate fit and opacity, and the prohibition of imitating disbelievers or immoral people. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that clothing cannot be specific to non-Muslims or those of bad character—whether in the garment itself, its color, or how it is worn—and illustrates this principle with examples ranging from religious symbols to tattoos and gang-related clothing styles. He stresses that Muslims must deliberately differentiate themselves through their appearance, and this applies even to private settings.
